title: How a SIP works, in plain language
summary: What actually happens each month when you invest through a SIP, how units and NAV work, a simple worked example, and what a SIP cannot do.

title: What NAV means, and what it doesn’t
summary: NAV is the price of one unit of a scheme. How it is worked out, why a low NAV is not a bargain, and where to find it.

title: SIP or lump sum? How to think about the choice
summary: A SIP and a lump sum are two ways of putting money in. Neither is always better. How they differ, a made-up example, and questions to ask yourself.

title: What a risk profile is, and why it matters
summary: Your risk profile describes how much risk you can take and how much you are comfortable taking. What it covers, and how it relates to a scheme’s riskometer.

title: Why an emergency fund comes before investing
summary: An emergency fund keeps a surprise from forcing you to sell investments at a bad time. What it is, how much people often keep, where it lives, and how to build one.

title: Retirement corpus: how to estimate what you might need
summary: A step-by-step way to estimate the corpus your spending may need on retirement day, with a made-up worked example and why small changes in assumptions matter so much.

title: Expense ratio explained: what you pay and why it matters
summary: The expense ratio is the yearly cost of running a scheme, already reflected in the NAV. What it covers, how small differences add up, and how to compare costs sensibly.

title: How to read a mutual fund factsheet, with a made-up example
summary: A factsheet is a monthly summary of a scheme. What each section tells you, what to look for, and how to read a performance table without being misled.

title: What KYC is, and how it works for mutual funds
summary: KYC is a one-time identity check you complete before your first mutual fund investment. What it involves, what you need, common problems, and how to stay safe.
